svg.title: Military Iron: The Hammer Is the Small Number
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-military-iron-landed-cost; chapter number: 4; title: Military Iron: The Hammer Is the Small Number; subtitle: Purchase, shipping, and missing-part costs on GovPlanet trucks; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: $800 to $9,000 at the hammer; a $9,000 LVSR swelled to $25,000 to $30,000 once missing ECUs and parts landed; buckets: label: Truck purchase price; low: 800; high: 9000; notes: Range of GovPlanet military trucks bought by Quentin.; label: LMTV shipping from Hawaii; low: 5000; high: 5000; notes: $800 bid, about $1,000 with fees, $6,000 in before seeing it in person.; label: Replacement doors; low: 6000; high: 6000; notes: Doors alone cost $6,000; ECUs, glass, and turret caps also get robbed.; label: CAT ECM; low: 600; high: 4000; notes: A $4,000 ECM turned up for $600 on Marketplace.; caption: Profit is locked in at the hammer: price every unknown leak as a roughly $10,000 valve body, because a $20,000 projected Landoll trailer profit ended at about $280.; assumptions note: Buckets are separate reported cost lines, not a single summed invoice; ranges reflect the low and high figures each practitioner gave.; note: Attributed to iron king productions (vlBL3apKXg0) and Casey LaDelle (XAvSq6gx5KQ).
